slides.title:
A store boss got
the president to
*move Thanksgiving.*
slides.sub: True story. And it didn't work 👇

slides.title:
shopping days before
*Christmas*, in 1939.
slides.sub:
Thanksgiving was the last Thursday
of November: Nov. 30 that year.
Holiday shopping only started after it
(Fortune, Time).

slides.title:
*Fred Lazarus Jr.*, boss of
Federated Department Stores.
slides.sub:
The group that became today's
Macy's, Inc. His family store in Ohio
had the first department-store
escalator in the US (Fortune, Wikipedia).

slides.title:
FDR moves Thanksgiving
*one week earlier.*
slides.sub:
Announced in August 1939. Retailers
asked for it, and Lazarus is credited
with convincing Roosevelt (Wikipedia,
Fortune). One more week to sell.

slides.title:
of Americans disapproved.
They called it *“Franksgiving.”*
slides.sub:
Gallup poll (via Mental Floss). 23 states
kept Nov. 30, 22 followed FDR (Time).
Football coaches, pastors and turkey
farmers were furious (Fortune).

slides.title: Merchants or no merchants, *I can't see any reason for changing it.*
slides.author:
Chairman of the board

slides.title:
That's how the *Wall Street
Journal* judged it in 1941.
slides.sub:
1939 and 1940 data: the extra week
gave no real boost to retail sales
(Mental Floss, Newspapers.com).

slides.title:
Thursday of November:
the rule *since 1942.*
slides.sub:
FDR signed the law on Dec. 26, 1941
(Newspapers.com). Black Friday still
follows that calendar. It's today.
